historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: guided 2026 volumes (2,375-2,450 Bcfe, +1-3%) plus ~1%/yr mid-cycle price drift; none of the CAGRs is usable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (24-35%) diverges from revenue and EPS CAGRs by far more than 30%, but the divergence is an artefact: equity jumped from share issuance for the Equitrans Midstream merger (Jul-2024, 445M -> 560M shares) and the Olympus acquisition, not from retained earnings. Revenue and FCF CAGRs are commodity-cycle artefacts (FY2020 trough at Henry Hub ~$2.0, FY2025 at ~$3.5). EPS 5yr is undefined (FY2020 EPS -3.68).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less equity-award taxes, consolidated): FY2020 467, FY2021 556, FY2022 1,973, FY2023 1,067, FY2024 312, FY2025 2,723 (attributable 2,271). SBC-adjusted and reported CAGRs are within 1pp of each other; SBC is not growing faster than cash flow. The series describes the gas price, not the business, which is why FY0 is treated as a mid-cycle year and the forward path is built from volumes, price and per-unit costs rather than from any CAGR.

scenario_narratives.base: A mid-cycle gas producer: FY2026 lands near guidance (2,375-2,450 Bcfe, ~$3.5B attributable FCF at the February strip including ~$600M of elected growth capex), then FY2027 revenue steps down as pricing normalises to a $3.50 Henry Hub with a $0.45 differential. From there EQT grows 2-3% a year: compression and MVP Boost/Southgate add 1-2% volume, premium power and LNG contracts add ~1% to realisations, per-unit costs drift down, and the cash tax shelter unwinds to a 22% rate by 2030. The Blackstone midstream JV takes its ~$450M/yr of distributions throughout; the model is attributable to EQT after that leakage.
scenario_narratives.bull: The structural gas-demand thesis plays out: LNG export capacity and Appalachian power demand hold Henry Hub above $4 for several years, basis tightens as MVP Boost and Transco expansions come on, and EQT's premium-priced supply deals convert that into a sustained 65% attributable margin with no FY2027 mean-reversion. Growth capex earns its keep and the JV Base Return is reached sooner.
scenario_narratives.bear: Gas oversupply returns in 2027: associated gas, delayed LNG trains and a full storage cycle push Henry Hub to $2.50-2.75 and Appalachian basis blows out. Revenue drops ~15%, the attributable margin falls to the low-50s, capex intensity rises because maintenance spend does not shrink with price, and FCF roughly halves. EQT survives comfortably on its balance sheet, but the equity is worth much less than today's price.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value EQT as a mid-cycle owner of a low-cost, integrated Appalachian gas system rather than off the trailing twelve months, which include a winter price spike. The flows are attributable to EQT after the Blackstone midstream JV's 60% distribution share, SBC and the cash tax withheld on awards are expensed, the cash tax shelter is unwound to a 22% rate over five years, and the terminal value is capped at 12x owner FCF because this is a commodity producer. Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and their weights, at a single 8.5% USD WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: Henry Hub price: every $0.25/MMBtu sustained change moves attributable EBITDA by roughly $500-550M on ~2,400 Bcfe net of the ~25% hedge book.
Appalachian basis: the FY2026 differential guide is $(0.35)-(0.55); a return to the $(0.80)+ differentials of 2023-24 is worth ~$1B of EBITDA.
Cash tax normalisation timing: the model ramps to 22% by 2030; if IDC expensing and bonus depreciation defer it further, value is understated, and vice versa.

Midstream JV leakage: ~$450M/yr goes to the Blackstone Class B holder until a ~$3.4B Base Return is reached; the model holds that leakage in the margin forever and gives no credit for the eventual step-up.
Growth capex discipline: $580-640M of 2026 growth capex is modelled as tapering; if elected growth spend becomes a permanent fixture, capex intensity stays ~2pp higher.
Share count: no buybacks despite a $2B authorisation, with ~1%/yr creep in the diluted count from awards; the flat count assumes SBC expensing covers this.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 47.94-68.24.
data_sources.financials: EQT_Metrics.csv (105 periods from core_metrics, SEC XBRL companyfacts); Q2-2026 10-Q (accession 0000033213-26-000043) for debt, cash, diluted shares, JV terms and NCI distributions; Q2-2026 earnings release (8-K 2026-07-21, EX-99.1) and Q4-2025 earnings release (8-K 2026-02-17, EX-99.1) for adjusted EBITDA attributable to EQT, free cash flow attributable to EQT, per-unit costs, hedges and 2026 guidance.
data_sources.qualitative: No EQT_Analysis.json existed at build time; scenario axes are drawn from the earnings releases (LNG offtake, CPV Shay power deal, MVP Boost/Southgate, compression programme, hedge book) and the FY2025 10-K reserves disclosure (28.0 Tcfe proved, PV-10 $26B at SEC pricing / $31B at strip).

inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares for Q2 2026 (629.049M, 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30, us-gaap:WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding). Cover-page basic count 625.5M at 2026-07-14. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging dilution as well would double-count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: share-based compensation add-back $60.8M (us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation) plus cash paid for taxes to net-settle share-based awards $54.2M (financing; us-gaap:PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation). EQT publishes no combined figure in its adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:03:28Z regular close (Friday); valuation written before the 2026-09-28 open
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.95 for a large-cap gas E&P gives cost of equity ~9.0%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.4% on $5.7B of senior notes (after-tax ~4.3% once the cash tax rate normalises); weights ~85% equity / 15% debt at an EV of ~$38B. Blended ~8.3%, rounded to 8.5%. Cyclicality is charged in the scenario flows and weights, NOT as a WACC premium, and all three scenarios use the same 8.5% (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP filer; operating leases are expensed inside operating costs and the operating lease liability is only $78M (FY2025 10-K), so no adjustment: lease liabilities are excluded from net debt and no separate lease charge is modelled.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged ONCE, in the flows. EQT consolidates PipeBox LLC (the Midstream JV, 49% economic / Class B held by a Blackstone Credit affiliate that receives 60% of JV distributions until a ~$3.4B Base Return is met) and Eureka Midstream (40% third party). The EBITDA margin path is built on adjusted EBITDA ATTRIBUTABLE to EQT (FY2025 $5,386M = 62.3% of revenue, versus $5,904M / 68.3% consolidated), and capex is likewise net of the NCI share. The $3,604.5M NCI book balance is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge. Cash check: FY2026 guided distributions to the JV NCI are $430-470M against ~$520M of NCI adjusted EBITDA less ~$70M NCI capex/contributions.
inputs.equity_method_treatment: The $3.9B equity-method stake (MVP Mainline Series A ~53%, LMM, MVP Southgate/Boost) is NOT added to the bridge because its cash distributions ($205-250M/yr guided) are inside adjusted EBITDA and its capital contributions ($150-170M in 2026) are inside the capex line. Excluded income needs its matching asset and vice versa; here both stay in the flows.
inputs.mid_cycle_basis: FY2025 is used as FY0 because it is close to a mid-cycle year: Henry Hub averaged ~$3.5/MMBtu, realised price $3.19/Mcfe on 2,382 Bcfe, and the year carried a $134M class-action charge. The trailing twelve months to June 2026 (revenue ~$9.5B, consolidated FCF ~$3.8B) include the Q1-2026 winter price spike and are NOT the base. Year-1 (FY2026) follows guidance and H1 actuals; FY2027 steps DOWN to a mid-cycle Henry Hub of ~$3.50 with a $0.45 differential before growing with volumes.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF on the mid-cycle route (dcf-methods SKILL routing row 'operating company, cyclical' + owner-fcf-adaptations (c) NCI and (f) risk-once). Owner FCF: reported_fcf here is the ATTRIBUTABLE cash-basis figure: consolidated OCF less capex $2,837.5M, less NCI adjusted EBITDA $518.6M, plus NCI share of capex/contributions $67.3M = $2,386M; less SBC incl. award taxes $115.0M = last_fcf $2,271M. Interest income is nil (net debt company). Buybacks: none in FY2024-FY2025 (PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock = 0) although a $2B authorisation exists; the flat share count is a modelling convention EQT is not yet funding, and the diluted count has crept ~1%/yr from awards. Cash tax: EQT has been a de-minimis cash taxpayer since 2019 (FY2025 cash taxes a $79M refund against $652M GAAP expense, $658M deferred) because of IDC expensing and bonus depreciation; the model RAMPS the cash rate to 22% by year 5 rather than perpetuating the shelter. Working capital capture is 0: EQT's working-capital swings are price- and hedge-margin-driven, not growth-driven. The 7.75% debentures ($115M current) were repaid after quarter end, which is net-debt neutral. Blackline Midstream ($77M, closed 2026-07-21) is immaterial and not modelled. Upside not modelled: the JV distribution split steps up in EQT's favour once the Blackstone Base Return (~$3.4B remaining) is achieved, roughly 7-8 years out.

bear.narrative: Henry Hub reverts to $2.50-2.75 from 2027: Permian associated gas keeps growing, LNG start-ups slip, a mild winter leaves storage full, and Appalachian basis widens again because takeaway lags supply; Homer City and CPV slip past 2028, so the premium-priced volumes that the market is already paying for do not arrive in the explicit horizon. EQT curtails volumes, growth capex is cut but maintenance capex is sticky per Mcfe, so capex intensity rises and the attributable margin falls to the low-50s. The cash tax ramp is slower only because there is less income. The balance sheet (net debt ~1x EBITDA, $3.6B liquidity) is not at risk, so the bear case is a value case, not a solvency case.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +7%: H1-2026 revenue $5,189M (+21% YoY on the Q1 winter spike) and a softer H2 at a ~$3.0-3.3 Henry Hub with 2,375-2,450 Bcfe guided. FY2027 -4%: step down to a mid-cycle $3.50 Henry Hub less a $0.45 differential on ~2,480 Bcfe plus $650-700M third-party midstream revenue. Thereafter 2-3%: 1-2%/yr volume growth from compression, MVP Boost/Southgate, the CPV Shay power deal (325,000 Dth/d) and the Homer City 4.4 GW AI/HPC campus deal (up to 665,000 MMBtu/d, PJM-linked pricing, targeted from 2027) and LNG offtake, plus ~1% price drift. Those contracts are modelled as volume growth and a slow realisation uplift, not as a step change, because their timing depends on counterparties' plants being built.
base.margin_rationale: Attributable adjusted EBITDA margin: FY2025 62.3% (63.8% ex the $134M class-action charge) at Henry Hub ~$3.5; H1-2026 69.6% on the spike; Q2-2026 ~59% at lower prices. FY2026 64% blends the two halves; mid-cycle 61% rising to 62% as guided per-unit costs fall from $1.15/Mcfe (2025) to $1.05-1.20 (2026) and premium power/LNG contracts replace in-basin sales.
base.capex_rationale: Attributable capex incl. JV contributions: FY2025 $2,340M (27.1%). FY2026 guided $2,770-3,000M consolidated (maintenance $2,040-2,190M, growth $580-640M, contributions $150-170M) less ~$70M NCI share = ~$2,815M = 30.5% of FY2026 revenue. Growth capex tapers after MVP Southgate completes at end-2026; long-run 28% = ~$2,300M maintenance plus a modest growth budget.
base.tax_rationale: Cash rate ramps 3% -> 22% over five years. FY2025 cash tax was a refund; deferred tax was $658M of $652M total expense. IDC expensing and OBBBA bonus depreciation defer, not eliminate, the liability; a perpetuated shelter would overstate value materially.
base.terminal_rationale: 2.0% terminal growth (below the 2.5% house default: finite resource, but >30 years of inventory). Cap 12x owner FCF, the cyclical setting: today's EV/attributable-FCF is ~13x on FY2025 and ~11x on 2026 guidance.

bull.narrative: Henry Hub holds $4.00-4.50 through 2027-2030 as Gulf Coast LNG trains (Plaquemines, Corpus Christi Stage 3, Golden Pass) and Appalachian data-centre/power demand absorb supply; Appalachian basis tightens as MVP Boost and Transco Southeast Expansion add takeaway; premium power-linked contracts (CPV Shay, Homer City, the 1.2 Bcf/d Southeast utility deals) arrive on schedule and lift realisations above in-basin pricing. Per-unit costs keep falling on 29,000-foot laterals and compression, holding the attributable margin at 65%. Revenue does not mean-revert in FY2027.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because the single dominant driver, the Henry Hub price, is genuinely two-sided and outside management's control; the bear case is a value case rather than a solvency case (net debt ~1x EBITDA, $3.6B liquidity), so it does not warrant 30%+. Bull cut to 25% because it needs several independent things to hold at once: LNG trains on schedule, Appalachian takeaway expansions, power-demand contracts landing, and a Henry Hub above the current five-year strip for most of the decade.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
